headline: Bone age
body: It's five axes pulling on the same clock at once.
punch: Which is why single-hormone thinking keeps producing wrong predictions.

headline: Most explanations
body: It's estrogen. It's growth hormone. It's thyroid. Each is describing one input to a system with several, then generalising from it.
punch: The clinical reviews don't have that luxury.

headline: The full complement
body: Growth hormone and IGF-1 drive proliferation and the growth velocity you actually see. They move height fast and bone age comparatively slowly.
punch: This is the axis that buys you time.

headline: Then thyroid hormone
body: Thyroid hormone is required for normal chondrocyte maturation. Too little and maturation stalls; too much and the whole schedule accelerates.
punch: Thyroid is the tempo control, not the volume.

headline: Estrogens
body: Estrogen is the dominant driver of skeletal maturation and eventual fusion — and androgens contribute substantially by being converted into it.
punch: This is the axis that spends your remaining time.

headline: Androgens
body: They increase growth velocity and accelerate skeletal maturation simultaneously. You get taller faster while having less time left to do it in.
punch: Two effects in opposite directions from one hormone.

headline: Which is why
body: Chronological age tells you how long you've existed. Bone age tells you how much growth capacity you have left — and only one of those is modifiable.
punch: Same age, different amounts of runway.

headline: And why the tradeoff
body: Anything that speeds growth velocity through the androgen axis also spends skeletal maturation. Optimising one number while ignoring the other is how people end up shorter.
punch: Growing faster and growing longer are competing goals.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms, real citations, no protocols.
